subject: Information Theory
title: The Information Superhighway
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Information Superhighway usable.

hook.text: In 1993, Al Gore predicted an 'information superhighway'. Thirty years later: Instagram, TikTok, and Zoom. Close enough?

buildup.text: Global internet traffic hit 5 zettabytes per year in 2022. That's every book ever written, every 36 seconds.

discovery.text: Shannon's 1948 paper made this possible. Every compression algorithm, every error-correcting code traces back to him.

twist.text: We're still nowhere near theoretical limits. Shannon showed the ceiling; engineering is still building the ladder.

climax.text: From telegraph wires to quantum channels, the story of networks is the story of approaching Shannon's limits.

punchline.text: One paper in 1948. Every network since stands on its shoulders.

quiz.question: What did Shannon's 1948 paper establish for networks?
options: Theoretical limits on information transmission that still guide engineering
